subject: Pricing / migration inquiry — price-match request and replacement evaluation
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@cloudforge.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T14:12:00Z
Subject: Looking for price match + migration plan (replacing CobaltAI)

Hi Sergio,

Were evaluating Redwood to replace our current inference vendor (CobaltAI). Our procurement team has asked whether Redwood can match the commercial terms we currently have in our Q1 SOW and provide a concrete migration plan. Quick context:

- Current vendor: CobaltAI (incumbent)
- Typical monthly tokens: ~1.6B (spiky ecom events)
- Current blended unit price: $0.0007 / token (includes committed discount + reserved capacity)
- Contract remaining: 7 months (auto-renews unless we sign a replacement)

Attached is our current SOW + usage summary. We're specifically asking:
1) Can Redwood match or beat the blended unit price?
2) What packaging do you recommend (hosted API vs dedicated capacity) given our traffic pattern?
3) What migration credits / operational assistance do you offer for a vendor switch?

Wed like a short proposal and a one-pager migration plan by next week if possible.

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Head of Procurement, CloudForge (on behalf of Apex Retail)

Attachments: Apex_current_SOW_Q1_2026.pdf, usage_summary_Q1_2026.csv

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@cloudforge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Looking for price match + migration plan (replacing CobaltAI)

Hi Elena — thanks for the context and the SOW. Ill loop in Marissa (AE) and Jordan (Solutions) to put together a short proposal. A few clarifying items so we can size the right packaging: 

- Is the 1.6B token figure a 30-day peak or a blended month? Any day-level peak reports you can share helps with latency/slot sizing.
- Are there strict data residency requirements or SOC 2 evidence youll need for vendor onboarding?
- Are you evaluating a 1:1 feature parity with CobaltAI (same model family) or are you open to a slightly different model + KV-cache strategy if it reduces cost?

Initial signals: we can often match pricing when customers commit to Dedicated (reserved capacity) for a 12 month term. If you prefer self-serve Hosted we can offer migration credits but matching blended token price on pure pay-as-you-go is harder. Ill ask Marissa to propose a price-match structure and Jordan to draft a migration checklist. Can we tentatively schedule a 30-min call on Thursday to review?

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Looking for price match + migration plan (replacing CobaltAI)

Sergio / Jordan — notes from my pricing review: 

- Goal: get to price parity while protecting unit economics. Per their SOW, blended $0.0007/token is aggressive but doable with a 12-mo reserved commit and a migration credit. Proposed structure: 
  * 12-month Dedicated commit (N GPUs / throughput to match peaks) + 10% off published reserved rate = ~match to $0.00068/token effective for forecasted billing tiers.
  * Migration package: one-time credit equal to 1 month of committed spend + 10 hours integration support from Solutions (Jordan).
  * SLA: 99.9% uptime + targeted latency SLOs; premium support add-on available for guaranteed response.

- Packaging note: if they prefer Hosted API to avoid infra ops, we can offer a blended hosted discount but it will need a slightly higher list price with a larger migration credit to offset.

- Docs to prepare: price_match_proposal PDF, migration roadmap doc, TCO comparison (Redwood vs CobaltAI). Jordan, can you sketch a two-phase migration (pilot + cutover) with estimated work effort?

Im comfortable green-lighting the price-match proposal above pending Sergios signoff.

– Marissa

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@cloudforge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-27T17:45:00Z
Subject: Price-match proposal and migration roadmap (proposal attached)

Elena — per our review, please find attached a concise proposal and a migration roadmap: Redwood_price_match_proposal_20260227.pdf (summary of commercial terms) and Migration_Roadmap_v1.docx. Key points below: 

- Offer (summary):
  * 12-month Dedicated Reserved commit to match peak throughput. Effective blended token price: $0.00068 (estimated) for forecasted tiers during contract term.
  * One-month committed-spend credit applied to first invoice (migration credit).
  * 10 hours of SRE/solutions integration support included for pilot + cutover.
  * Standard SLA: 99.9% uptime; SLA credits defined in proposal.

- Packaging recommendation: start with a 6-week pilot on a Dedicated pool sized to handle 60% of peak traffic (to validate caching/latency). If pilot meets SLOs, scale to full commit and apply credits. Pilot plan is in the attached roadmap (phase 1: pilot, phase 2: validation, phase 3: cutover + rollback runbook).

- Commercial items that will require confirmation: exact commit level (GPU count / reserved QPS), data residency requirement, and whether Apex needs HSM/KMS integration.

If youre comfortable with this high-level offer I can push a DocuSign link for signature. Ive also attached a TCO sheet for Apex vs CobaltAI.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a call to walk through the attachments.

On Thu, Feb 25, 2026 at 3:03 PM, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com> wrote:

> - Are you evaluating a 1:1 feature parity with CobaltAI (same model family) or are you open to a slightly different model + KV-cache strategy if it reduces cost?

Best,
Sergio

Attachments: Redwood_price_match_proposal_20260227.pdf, Migration_Roadmap_v1.docx

From: Elena Morris <elena@cloudforge.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@apexretail.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Price-match proposal and migration roadmap (proposal attached)

Sergio / Marissa / Jordan — thank you, this looks promising. A few quick items before we proceed to signature: 

- Can you confirm the SLA credit formula (example scenarios) and whether the 99.9% covers regional failover? We need clear language for business-critical event windows.
- Data residency: Apex requires EU + US regional isolation for PII processing during peak sales events. Do you support region pinning for workloads?
- DocuSign: please send the signature link and well route through procurement once legal signs off on a quick review.

If you can confirm the two items above and send the DocuSign link, Ill get this through procurement this week. Raj will be the internal owner from Apex.

Best,
Elena
